request.spec:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each user can now pick which people-list columns their screen shows. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec, and `tsc --noEmit` reports no type errors.

**How it works**
- **Where the choice lives:** the switched-off columns are kept in a `hiddenColumns` value in the screen's URL, the same way the list's sort order already works. That makes the choice belong to one user's screen only. It stays in place when the sheet is re-loaded, and other users' screens are unaffected. Because it isn't saved on the server, it won't carry over to a new browser session or tab. The spec only needs it to last while the screen stays open.
- **The checkboxes:** a new "Columns" box sits just above the people table, with one checkbox per column, each tagged `column-<name>` (`features/columns/chooser.slot.tsx`). The list of columns and the hooks that read and set the choice are in `features/columns/columns.ts`.
- **I added `excess` to your list.** The spec switches off `excess` and expects its cells to disappear, so it gets a checkbox even though the change request doesn't name it.
- **Switching a column off:** its cells disappear, and so does its table header so the columns stay lined up. The person-list totals, the app header, the summary and every other figure are worked out as before. The files changed are `claimed`, `due` (due-total and excess), `overdue`, `hold`, `retire`, `aliases`, `statement` and `patrons`, plus the people list itself for terms and contact.

**Choices worth checking**
- **Action buttons go with their column.** The hold, retired and aliases cells also hold that column's buttons and date fields, such as Hold and Retire. Switching the column off hides those too, since "no cell at all" covers the whole cell.
- **Columns that share a cell.** The three statement figures are in one cell, and so are patrons and backing. Switching one off removes just that value. The cell, and its Statement or Patron controls, only disappears when all of its columns are off.

There's no checkbox for name, grade or tags, or for snapshots, clashing or the other columns the request doesn't name.
